security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD S-mode kernel probes has_sstc=true (ISA string), unconditionally writes stimecmp CSR directly, but M-mode firmware has not set menvcfg.STCE=1, so stimecmp writes do not generate the STIP timer interrupt signal — the kernel assumes the spec's read-only-STIP-reflects-stimecmp semantic but the hardware still operates in writable-STIP legacy mode.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: has_sstc && csr_write(stimecmp, without menvcfg.STCE verification in S-mode
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD gates direct stimecmp access on has_sstc but never verifies menvcfg.STCE; if firmware leaves SSTC disabled, timer interrupts silently fail and the scheduler starves

findings.finding: has_sstc is set purely from the ISA string's 'sstc' extension substring, with no verification that M-mode firmware has set menvcfg.STCE=1. The S-mode kernel cannot read menvcfg directly, so it blindly trusts the ISA string. Per the RISC-V spec (machine.adoc:2233-2239), when SSTC is implemented but STCE=0, any S-mode access to stimecmp raises an illegal-instruction exception. On such a platform, the kernel will panic when set_timecmp() or riscv_timer_intr() first writes stimecmp.

spec_citations.excerpt: The Sstc extension adds the STCE (STimecmp Enable) bit to menvcfg CSR. When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception, STCE in henvcfg is read-only zero, and STIP in mip and sip reverts to its defined behavior as if this extension is not implemented.

When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp or vstimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception, STCE in henvcfg is read-only zero, and STIP in mip and sip reverts to its defined behavior as if this extension is not implemented.

findings.finding: Unconditionally writes stimecmp CSR when has_sstc is true, without any runtime probe or verification that the CSR access will succeed. If menvcfg.STCE=0 (firmware not configured), the csr_write(stimecmp, timecmp) raises an illegal-instruction exception per the spec, resulting in kernel panic at trap.c:366-369. This is called from riscv_timer_et_start() on every timer event setup, making it a hard boot-time or first-timer-event crash on affected platforms.

spec_citations.excerpt: The STCE bit enables stimecmp for S-mode when set to one. When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception...

findings.finding: Same unconditional stimecmp write pattern in the timer interrupt handler: writes stimecmp = -1UL when has_sstc is true with no STCE verification. If the firmware enabled STCE=1 at boot but later cleared it (theoretical), or if the kernel booted on a platform where the ISA string advertises SSTC but menvcfg.STCE remains 0, every timer interrupt would cause a panic on the illegal-instruction exception.

findings.finding: The S-mode illegal-instruction handler unconditionally panics the kernel. There is no recovery path for a failed stimecmp access. If the first stimecmp write from set_timecmp() raises an illegal-instruction exception (due to STCE=0), the kernel crashes with 'Illegal instruction' panic. A robust implementation would probe stimecmp accessibility at boot time and fall back to the SBI timer path if the access fails, rather than crashing the kernel.
